questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Being relevant to my degree (English-speaking country), having a culture, history, and nature that interested me and being easy to get to.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lots of unique experiences and new opportunities to explore a new culture and country and experience a new university, teaching methods, and different way of assessing work.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find the information, but there was a lot of information to stay take in, which made it overwhelming.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: E-mails from the university with exchange student events and I got assigned a specific person at the university I could write to with any questions relating to my exchange.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy finding the campus housing that was available to me, but it was extremely stressful waiting for the reply and looking for accommodations elsewhere in the meantime, and I know that not everyone who applied for accommodation through the university got it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That is helps a lot to call in to the student accommodation to talk to them, rather than just wait for a reply over e-mail.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is extremely expensive (almost 2x the amount of rent I normally pay), but the room is very nice and it feels safe living here. It is inconvenient that there are no kitchen items in the kitchen and that there are no groups or other facilities for exchange students to exchange things such at kitchen items and bedding, as it is something everyone will have to buy and then donate – where it would be a lot smarter if exchange students could leave their things for future exchange students to benefit from.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I do not remember it in details, but I just had to follow instructions I got through e-mails and fill out some personal information about myself and my study and write by course wishes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were e-mails I could write to, though I did not do this.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky and got all of my first choices, however I know this is far from the case for everyone.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the instructions you are given and do it as soon as it is possible, to hopefylly register for the classes you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: One course was not the level of academia I expected (it was a first year course though) and the lectures in that course were not very satisfying, but I was very happy with the two other courses I took.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took on 1st year course and two courses that could be taken either on 3rd or 4th year.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was pretty similar with lecture-like classes and sometimes group-work. The tutorials were quite different though, with quite small classes (12-ish people) and a more assignment-like structure where we went through one problem or question either on the class or in smaller groups.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociolinguistics
Scots and Scottish English
Linguistics and the English Language 1A

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sociolinguistics and Scots and Scottish English I really enjoyed, but I think it could have been fun taking a course focusing more on the history of Scotland/Edinburgh or a culture-study or something like that they only offer to exchange student i.e. then you know that it will probably be interesting for exchange students and a great way to meet other exchange students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Having to buy everything I needed for the kitchen and bedding.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think the prices are similar to Denmark, maybe a little cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not join any societies, but there were loads to choose between.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of sport clubs, social clubs etc., weekly parties, dances etc. really anything you could think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Joining the Erasmus-activities, and going to a lot of things in the intro week.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Isle of Skye, Glasgow, the turisty things in Edinburgh. There are a lot of groups tours specially for exchange students that you can book.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, it is not that different from Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was a lot easier for me since I lived in student accommodation with other local students, but if you are up for it just try to speak with people in your lectures and tutorials!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: How different written exams and assessment is here. Other cultural differences were more fun than challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How welcoming everyone is and the many things to experience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It is expensive to go on exchange so save for it, search for housing in good time, research as much as you can before you go so there are less stressful things to figure out when you get there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: That the written exams are handwritten and that there is nothing in the kitchen if you get student accomodation.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of new people, challenging myself and getting to experience so much of Scotland.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to do a lot of things by myself and not have my support network from home close by in hard times.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
